title: Tensor construction bounds before canonicalization
finding: The experimental tensor contract checked axis-label, axis-count and entry-count ceilings only after sorting or tuple conversion on some construction paths. That bounded retained state but did not bound work or memory consumed while canonicalizing oversized caller input.
primary_claim: Every high-cardinality tensor construction surface now refuses an oversized or unsized input before iterating, sorting or copying its elements.
acceptance: axis label count is checked before _sorted_strings can iterate or sort labels
coordinate count is checked before coordinate parsing
TensorView axis count is checked before tuple construction
TensorView entry count is checked before tuple construction
unsized iterables are refused rather than consumed without a mechanical ceiling
normal sequence-based canonical contracts retain the existing deterministic representation

adversarial_evidence.strategy: ExplodingSequence exposes length but raises on every element access; each oversized case must refuse while accessed remains false

requested: PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest -q tests/twin/test_tensor_construction_bounds.py tests/twin/test_tensor_kernel.py tests/twin/test_fourfold_contracts.py tests/twin/test_projection_verifier.py
verification.claim: source-level hardening and focused regression preparation only; no green test or performance claim without executed exact-head evidence

rollback: Revert this packet without changing the canonical Fourfold/Forest contracts; the tensor module remains an isolated experimental projection.
